text: Puntsagiin Jasrai (Mongolian: Пунцагийн Жасрай; 26 November 1933 – 25 October 2007) was a Mongolian politician who served as Prime Minister of Mongolia from 21 July 1992 until 19 July 1996. He was born in 1933 in the sum (district) of Bugat in the Govi-Altai Province and graduated from high school in Tonkhil district of Govi-Altai Province in 1950. He worked as an Education inspector from 1950 to 1956 and joined the Mongolian People's Revolutionary Party (MPRP) in 1951. In 1961, he earned a degree in agricultural economics from the Moscow Higher School of Economics. From 1970 to 1975, he served as chairman of the State Prices Committee. In 1973, he was elected a deputy of the State Great Khural for the first of four times, from 1973 to 1986. From 1976 to 1978, he was head of the planning and finance department of the MPRP Central Committee. In 1978, he became first deputy chairman of the State Planning Commission and in 1984 was appointed deputy chairman of the Council of Ministers. In 1988, he became first deputy chairman of the Council of Ministers and was elected a candidate member of the Politburo in 1989. In the mid-1980s, Jasrai became one of Mongolia's earliest proponents of free market reforms. With the collapse of communist power in 1990, he resigned from his government and party posts and became president of the Association of Mongolian Production and Services Cooperatives, where he made several consultative visits to foreign countries, establishing important economic contacts. He was known for being straightforward and honest. On June 28, 1992, Jasrai was elected to the Mongolian State Great Hural representing constituency 26 in Ulaanbaatar. At the Hural's first session on 20 July 1992, he was appointed prime minister. Before the selection, he stated he was "not a politician, rather a simple Economist" and promised to work toward expanding economic development and democracy in Mongolia. In June 1993, he visited the United States, meeting with government representatives, participating in an economic symposium, and engaging with World Bank and International Monetary Fund representatives, as well as speaking at the National Press Club. In summer 1993, opposition parties strongly criticized Jasrai and his government for failing to prevent economic deterioration and continued calls for his resignation throughout his term. They later formed the Mongolian Democratic Union coalition. In the July 1996 parliamentary elections, the Democratic Union won, marking the first non-MPRP government since Mongolia's independence in 1921, and Mendsaikhany Enkhsaikhan was appointed Prime Minister. Jasrai retained his seat in the State Great Hural until 2004. He died on 25 October 2007 in Ulan Bator at the age of 73.
